_readme: The headless smoke gate: does the game boot, does the player move, does a wall stop
it? Three things no unit test can answer, because all three need the real physics
server, the real input map and the real map data at once.
It walks NORTH rather than east: the town's east side is a gate to another map now,
and a test that walks into it would be testing the warp instead. Worth noting how
that surfaced - opening the gate broke this gate, loudly, on the run after the map
changed. A smoke test pinned to level content will keep doing that.
Nothing here names a coordinate. Asserting 'y decreased' survives someone tuning
walk_speed; asserting 'y == 24.0' does not, and a test that breaks on a tuning
change is a test people learn to edit rather than read.

steps.text: keep going until the north wall stops us
and the wall does not trap us - we can walk back
